prompt:
Create a transparent 2 by 2 animation key-pose sheet showing one fantasy RPG character performing a SOLO two-handed sweeping hammer movement exercise. Four separate full-body cels in reading order, no writing, scenery, other people, ground, dust, glow, motion blur or arc effects. Generous transparent gutters and margins; entire long tool and both feet visible in each cel.
REFERENCE ROLES: image 1 (four realistic figures) is the exact BODY MOVEMENT reference. Image 2 (four illustrated poses) is the approved CHARACTER IDENTITY, proportions, outfit, face, rendering style, and hammer design reference. This is a NEW sweeping action for that SAME illustrated character. Do not copy the downward planted-tool ending from image 2. Preserve the much broader cross-body swing and the follow-through of image 1.
Detailed hand-painted chibi wuxia RPG character: strong bearded man, red-brown ponytail and red ribbons, purple-brown fur-trimmed coat and boots, red cloth sash, bronze wrist guards, large rectangular purple iron hammer with bronze bands and wooden handle. Keep character head, torso, arms, hammer-head dimensions and handle length constant in ALL four poses. Same slightly elevated three-quarter game camera, facing front-right. No per-pose shrinking. Two feet planted in a wide stance, deliberate hip/shoulder rotation instead of rotating a frozen standing picture.
The wooden handle is long enough for both hands: approximately the same medium-long handle as image 2. Exactly TWO hands, both gripping the SAME continuous handle, anatomically connected arms, close grip near the butt during the swing, natural wrists. No hand at the hammer head, no extra forearms, no separated hands floating off the handle.
Top-left = first person of image 1. Low preparation: hammer head low behind the left side of the silhouette around knee height, shaft mostly across the waist. Knees flexed, shoulders turned, two hands in front of the waist, preparing to lift across the body.
Top-right = second person of image 1. Loaded shoulder position: bring BOTH hands close together beside and ABOVE the right shoulder/temple. Hammer head is high behind the body on the upper-left of the silhouette, handle diagonally across behind the crown. Torso coils and weight on rear leg. This is a shoulder-loaded wind-up, not a symmetrical overhead weightlifting pose.
Bottom-left = third person of image 1. Sweeping forward across the front: both arms extend together toward front-right around chest height, head of hammer far out in front-right/high-right; hips, chest and shoulders turn forcefully in the same direction. The sweeping plane is diagonal ACROSS THE BODY, not straight vertical down into the floor.
Bottom-right = fourth person of image 1. Follow through ACROSS THE BODY toward the opposite low LEFT side: hammer head ends low on the LEFT of the silhouette near the outside of the left knee, shaft crosses diagonally UP-RIGHT to the two hands near the RIGHT hip/waist. Torso rotated, knees flexed, weight transferred to front leg, head looking along the path. Hands remain on the butt. Tool head is suspended LOW BESIDE the leg, NOT planted on the ground, not hanging vertically under the fists. Show a wide readable cross-body arc from shoulder to opposite low side.
Four genuinely distinct poses matching the photo sequence, with consistent body and rigid hammer proportions. No invented overhead ground-contact finish.
